{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABZhuziw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhDIpac", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 79, "title": "Implement µPD765 non-DMA READ DATA with byte handshaking and interrupts", "body": "## Problem

Guest software cannot read floppy payloads through programmed I/O. At baseline `ae6b96926ce9146de9dbdfd1269686b74ae3a643`, `SPECIFY` is accepted but its parameters are discarded. READ DATA requires DMA channel 2 and transfers its payload atomically; port `0092h` exposes only result bytes. Software selecting non-DMA operation therefore receives DMA errors instead of execution-phase data.

This is one bounded FDC implementation task: add the non-DMA READ DATA execution path and its necessary command/status/interrupt lifecycle.

## Expected outcome

On VM and Ap, `SPECIFY` opcode `03h`, with ND set in the last parameter, selects non-DMA operation for subsequent supported READ DATA commands. ND clear retains the existing DMA path. Implement single-head MFM reads (`46h`, MT=0, SK=0), sequential sectors through EOT, and N=1–3 on existing supported media.

The controller contract is:

- During non-DMA execution, MSR EXM bit 5 and CB bit 4 are set. DIO bit 6 selects controller-to-CPU transfer; RQM bit 7 indicates byte availability. Payload reads consume one available byte. Status reads do not consume payload. Result phase clears EXM, and draining all seven results releases CB. See [NEC µPD765A/B datasheet, Tables 2–4](https://hxc2001.com/download/datasheet/floppy/thirdparty/FDC/NEC/UPD765_Datasheet_OCRed.pdf#page=9).
- Available execution bytes generate data interrupts. Reading the data register acknowledges that byte request. Command termination generates a result interrupt, acknowledged by reading the first result byte. Preserve the repository's slave IR3/master IR7 routing and ordinary EOI handling. See [NEC µPD765 specification, processor interface](https://www.scribd.com/document/1067140199/UPD765) and [NEC Application Note 8, processor interface and command sequences](https://hxc2001.com/download/datasheet/floppy/thirdparty/FDC/NEC/uPD765_App_Note_Mar79.pdf#page=4).
- PIO consumes no DMA address/count, mask or terminal-count state. Byte availability and service deadlines advance with guest clocks. An unserviced byte must terminate with abnormal ST0 and ST1.OR; repeated host reads must not manufacture clock progress. The [NEC status definitions](https://hxc2001.com/download/datasheet/floppy/thirdparty/FDC/NEC/UPD765_Datasheet_OCRed.pdf#page=10) define OR, while [Application Note 8](https://hxc2001.com/download/datasheet/floppy/thirdparty/FDC/NEC/uPD765_App_Note_Mar79.pdf#page=2) documents MFM service timing. Document the deterministic scheduling approximation and its conversion to the existing 8 MHz guest clock.
- Transfer only the requested single-head sector sequence through EOT, then expose `ST0, ST1, ST2, C, H, R, N` in order. Distinguish EOT termination without TC from successful TC termination; do not reuse a processor/TC-termination CHRN table for a different termination case. Pin the result expectations against the [NEC READ DATA functional description and result table](https://www.scribd.com/document/1067140199/UPD765).

Use the currently supported board-control setup (`0094h=18h`) for this bounded contract. Comprehensive external-control decoding is separate remaining work.

Non-goals: PIO WRITE DATA; deleted-data, format, scan or diagnostic commands; MT/head switching; N=0/DTL transfers; new TC/EOP injection; mechanical/flux timing; new media formats; comprehensive FDC board-control or error fidelity. Unsupported non-DMA commands must not silently execute DMA transfers.

## Context and reproduction

Source evidence:

- [Fdc state, status synthesis and command lengths](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/ae6b96926ce9146de9dbdfd1269686b74ae3a643/src/devices.rs#L768) contain no ND setting or payload execution state.
- [Bus FDC command execution](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/ae6b96926ce9146de9dbdfd1269686b74ae3a643/src/bus.rs#L794) discards SPECIFY and requires DMA eligibility for reads.
- [Existing DMA/FDC tests](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/ae6b96926ce9146de9dbdfd1269686b74ae3a643/tests/dma.rs#L340) cover auto-init, master-clear retention and controller disable. [PIC polling acceptance](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/ae6b96926ce9146de9dbdfd1269686b74ae3a643/tests/pic.rs#L947) exercises FDC READ ID through the cascade.

Minimal new regression: insert original patterned media, select `0094h=18h`, mask DMA channel 2, send `03h, DFh, 03h`, then issue a valid `46h` command. The baseline ignores ND and returns an overrun result. Expected: execution-phase payload becomes readable through `0092h`, independently of DMA eligibility.

Project progress: the inspected PR #78 bus diff adds IDE input-edge tracking, including synchronous command acceptance. The Coordinator reports 314 native integration tests and 106 production-Wasm browser cases passing; independent review and remote CI results were not supplied. This evaluator read source, the diff and reports and executed no acceptance tests. Missing local fixtures are not a project-level blocker.

All 26 inventory categories retain their supplied scope and status:

| Status | Categories |
| --- | --- |
| partial | cpu-v30, cpu386, protected-mode, memory, pic, pit, dma, rtc, keyboard, mouse, fdc, ide, gdc, egc, pegc, text-cg, display-timing, opn, opna, pcm86, bios, lio, integration |
| unimplemented | paging, fpu |
| implemented_unverified | grcg |

FDC remains partial after this Issue. PIO writes, multi-track transfers, format/scan operations, fuller SPECIFY timing, broader status/error contracts, external controls and comprehensive media/boot acceptance remain outstanding. Protected execution, paging and basic x87 remain fixed required work. Limited probes and existing game reports establish neither complete hardware accuracy nor commercial compatibility.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add focused raw-port Rust regressions for both profiles. Demonstrate a new ND=1 payload/EXM test failing on the baseline, then passing with implementation. Tests must drive commands, port accesses and guest clocks rather than inject payload state or PIC requests.
- [ ] Check single-sector and multi-sector reads through EOT, both heads independently with MT=0, and N=1/2/3 using original raw/D88 media within existing parser support. Compare every payload byte, complete result records and guards. Record the source derivation for exact result bytes, especially EOT without TC.
- [ ] Check MSR transitions before availability, during execution, between bytes and throughout all seven results. Early or wrong-direction accesses must not advance the transfer or corrupt the next command. Compare equivalent clock partitions, including an unserviced-byte deadline crossing, to catch batch-size-dependent behavior.
- [ ] Prove DMA independence with channel 2 masked and with the DMA controller disabled. Preserve its current/base addresses and counts, mode, bank, masks, status and shared byte pointer. After clearing ND, demonstrate existing DMA reads and writes still work.
- [ ] Verify data-request acknowledgement, held-request silence after PIC acknowledgement/EOI, subsequent byte requests and the separate result interrupt. Exercise actual CPU delivery and cascade ISR/EOI behavior. Cover overrun, unavailable sector/media, reset during execution and recovery through fresh SPECIFY/READ commands. No stale payload or result may leak into recovery.
- [ ] Add an original MIT source-built boot probe, offline builder and checked provenance manifest. Pin source, assembly command, synthetic firmware/image hashes, expected results, guards and a budget no greater than 2,000,000 scheduler slots per boot. The guest must issue raw FDC commands, validate payload, distinguish data/result interrupts in an actual INT 13h handler and report PASS only after its checks succeed.
- [ ] Boot the identical probe natively and in production release Wasm on VM and Ap, before/after Machine reset and at both `/` and `/pc98-rust/`. Require exact result/guard bytes, complete unchanged exported media, zero writes, bounded completion and no guest/core/browser errors. The host may step and inspect; it must not supply guest results.
- [ ] The Coordinator prepares original/licensed source-built fixtures and runs focused FDC tests plus `cargo test --locked --test core --test dma --test pic`, followed by `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `git diff --check` and `npm test`, following README prerequisites. Preserve existing DOS/apps/VM/audio, IDE-edge and six-game regressions, assertions and budgets. Record exact outcomes and any failures or unperformed checks honestly.
- [ ] Update hardware documentation and validation evidence with the implemented subset, scheduling policy and remaining gaps. Preserve all inventory categories and avoid a full-FDC compatibility claim. Complete repository-required PR review and revisions before merge. No commercial ROMs or proprietary guest media are required.

## Optional validation

None.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
